title: Serve-band assurance and autoscale governance language
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Purpose: Define contract language and measurable definitions for 'serve-bands' (a discrete capacity guarantee unit), a correlated error-budget model, and a corresponding autoscale governance policy that will be embedded in Dedicated contracts and the Console. Outcomes: 1) a guard-railed autoscale policy (min/max, burst rules, cool-downs, and proportional crediting), 2) formal SLA clauses expressing measurable serve-band availability and latency corridors, 3) an error-budget computation and credit formula suitable for invoicing and contractual remediation, and 4) a developer-friendly console UX that surfaces current band usage, burn rate, and predicted credit exposure.
acceptance_criteria: Legal has approved contract language for serve-band availability, definition of measurement windows, and credit calculation
Eng has implemented the autoscale policy knobs and exposed the telemetry used to compute serve-band availability
Billing computes credits automatically based on documented formula and exposes projected credit in Console
Console shows per-customer serve-band burn rate, current entitlement vs. realized throughput, and a predicted credit estimate with >=95% accuracy in staging
comments: 2026-02-15 - Aisha Patel: Ticket created after sync with sales/solutions — customers ask for deterministic capacity guarantees that map to predictable credits. Proposed name: 'serve-band' to avoid confusion with tokens or raw GPU hours.

2026-02-18 - Miguel Hernandez: Drafted three conceptual models: (A) Percentile-based availability over 30/90d windows, (B) Windowed throughput floors (quantiles by slice), (C) Hybrid serve-band where throughput and p95 latency are jointly tracked. Leaning to (C) because customers want both throughput and latency commitments. See Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/dedicated/serve-band-models

2026-02-22 - Grace Lin (Legal): Reviewed initial draft. Key asks: unambiguous measurement intervals, notice windows, and a remediation ladder (credits -> service credits -> termination triggers). Legal requests explicit language for 'force majeure' and 'capacity exhaustion events'. Added to draft: measurement anchor (UTC-based), sample rate, and allowed measurement exclusions. Document link: drive.google.com/drive/folders/1ServeBandLegal

2026-02-26 - Eng triage (Ethan Walker, Priya Rao): Feasibility notes: need a telemetry pipeline producing per-customer minute-level QPS and p95 latency for every model variant and AZ. Autoscale feasibility: we can support min/max pool sizing and burst tokens via current autoscaler but need two changes: (1) enforce proportional bleed when autoscale fails to provision, (2) add cooldown exceptions for multi-AZ failover. Created engineering ticket ENG-22903 to add required telemetry hooks and autoscale policy flags.

2026-03-02 - Miguel Hernandez: Posted proposed contract language snippet for serve-band availability and credit formula to PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/contracts/pull/287. Snippet summary: 'A serve-band is an entitlement to X sustained RPS (or token throughput) for a given model family and region. Measured over a rolling 30-day window; service credit applies when realized serve falls below 99.5% of entitlement aggregated by minute. Credit = max(0, (entitlement - realized)/entitlement) * monthly fee * scaling-factor(traffic-sensitivity)'. Requested legal feedback on scaling-factor semantics.

2026-03-05 - Legal (Grace Lin): Requested removal of ambiguous 'scaling-factor' and replacement with 'customer-class multiplier' defined in Appendix A. Proposed explicit caller-experience thresholds for p95 latency corridors (e.g., p95 < 150ms for 'interactive' band). Asked PM to draft appendix mapping customer classes to multipliers. Action: PM to create appendix and cross-reference release schedule.

2026-03-07 - UX (Jordan Kim): Early mockups for Console visualization submitted. Key screens: Serve-band overview card (entitlement, realized, burn rate), timeline with rolling 30d shutter, and 'what-if' slider to show projected credits if current burn rate persists. Mockups: https://drive.google.com/file/d/ServeBandConsoleMock

2026-03-08 - Engineering update (Ethan Walker): Telemetry pipeline prototype complete in staging. Provides per-minute metrics with customer_id, model_family, region, and p95 latency. Autoscaler flags added: 'guarantee_min' and 'burst_tokens' implemented. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1452. Note: staging shows ~3% variance in minute-level aggregation due to delayed logs; we recommend using 5-minute rollups for production measurements to reduce noise.

2026-03-10 - PM decision (Miguel Hernandez): Adopt 5-minute aggregation for measurement anchor to stabilize credit calculations. Update contract language to use '5-minute samples aggregated over rolling 30-day window'. Noted trade-off: small transient breaches may be smoothed — acceptable to customers seeking predictable billing.

2026-03-11 - Finance (Lena Ortiz): Reviewed credit impact model. Proposed safety cap: monthly credits capped at 30% of committed fee to limit revenue exposure while keeping customer protection meaningful. Action: add cap clause to contract and surface 'max potential credit' in Console projections.

2026-03-12 - Miguel Hernandez: Incorporated legal and finance feedback; updated draft contract language in PR and Confluence. Requested design + eng review for final iteration before stakeholder sign-off. Next steps: cross-team review meeting 2026-03-16, finalize appendix mapping customer-class multipliers, and stage the Console telemetry dashboard behind an opt-in toggle for GA customers. Linked artifacts: Confluence spec https://confluence.redwood.ai/dedicated/serve-band-spec, Contract PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/contracts/pull/287, Runtime PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1452

2026-03-12 - Miguel Hernandez: Notes on unresolved trade-offs: (1) Burst handling during cold-start of dedicated pool (we propose proportional throttling to avoid noisy neighbor), (2) Multi-region failover measurement (we will exclude full-region outages under 'declared platform outage' clause), (3) Whether p95 latency should be a hard requirement vs. advisory corridor (legal prefers advisory corridor tied to credit scale). Need final decision at cross-team review.
